header.userPrompt:
Implement GitHub issue #130 phase 3: reconcile subscription charges against real activity. Read issue #130 and closed issue #166 (phase 2, shipped in PR #169) first; the subscription model (terms, cancel/resume, extra charges, merchant link, EveryNMonths cadence, CardAutoCharge) already exists under server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/{actions/subscriptions,repositories}, controllers/SubscriptionsController.scala, lib/api/shared, and web/.../pages/subscriptions. The repo is PUBLIC: no PII anywhere (no real names, amounts, account digits) in code, tests, commits, PR text.

## Decisions already made (do not revisit)
1. Build ONE shared, pure, unit-testable date+amount matcher (a small service/object, no DB or HTTP inside) that scores/selects candidates by amount within a range, date within a tolerance window, and an optional merchant hint. Design it generically (candidate = date, amount, optional merchantId, id) so row-to-receipt matching can reuse it later, but only wire it to subscriptions now.
2. Tolerance window is a single server config value (see SubscriptionsConfig.scala for how config is done; default 5 days either side of the due date), not per subscription.
3. Reconciliation is DERIVED ON READ, not stored: for each subscription, expand the due dates inside the term(s) covering them (reuse the existing cadence/due-date logic; no drift for Monthly/Yearly/EveryNMonths; skip gaps between terms, so cancelled periods are never flagged), and match each due date against the user's expenses and bank statement rows. Per cycle status: Matched (with the matched expense/row id and actual date, flagged Late when outside the due date but inside tolerance), Retried (more than one matching charge attempt in the window), Missing (due date + tolerance passed with no match), Upcoming. Tie-break between two subscriptions with the same amount: prefer the one whose merchant matches the candidate, then the closest date; one charge may satisfy only one cycle (no double use).
4. The only persisted state is a manual payment log, for cash/portal/manual-transfer subscriptions that never produce a bank row: new table (next evolution number after the latest in the evolutions dir, follow existing evolution conventions, no DB CHECK constraints, FK to subscription ON DELETE CASCADE, user_id column) with subscription id, paid date, amount, optional note. A manual payment satisfies the cycle it falls in and counts as Matched.
5. Out of scope: term suggestions, receipt matching, any change to the existing subscription create/update behaviour.

## Deliverables
- Server: matcher; reconciliation action (get reconciliation for the user's subscriptions, optional single subscription); actions to add and delete a manual payment; repository/DAO for the log. Every query (read and write) has WHERE user_id = ?, every list query has ORDER BY, multi-step writes in a transaction. Limits: max 500 manual payments per subscription, note max 255 chars, amount positive and bounded like other subscription amounts. Validation at app level via the existing validated primitives (lib/common models, `.trusted` only in tests and DAO row parsing).
- Tapir endpoints in lib/api/shared, wired in ApiRouter and a controller; controller tests cover auth and encoding only, behaviour is tested in action integration tests using the real Postgres PostgresSpec pattern with random globally-unique data and no external calls. Matcher gets thorough pure unit tests (window edges, late, retried, missing, same-amount collision, gaps between terms, no double use, EveryNMonths and yearly cadence).
- MCP: extend the read-only subscriptions MCP surface (McpTools/McpDispatcher) with a `subscription_reconciliation` read tool returning the per-cycle statuses.
- Web: show per-subscription reconciliation on the existing SubscriptionsPage (missing / late / retried cycles clearly visible, matched ones collapsed), and a validated form to log/delete a manual payment. Every web form field must be a FormField over a validated primitive (see .orca/reviewers/frontend.md; mirror the existing Subscription*FormData and ui/forms primitives, extend ExpLocalDate/PositiveBigDecimal usage, no raw strings). No new route is needed; keep it reachable from the subscriptions page.
- Run scalafmtAll and scalafmtSbt, add specs, satisfy all .orca/reviewers gates. Commit per logical piece and open a PR.

resultJson.description:
Phase 3 of issue #130 (after #166/PR #169): show for each subscription whether every expected charge actually happened. For each subscription, the due dates inside its term(s) are expanded with the existing cadence rules: Monthly, Yearly, EveryNMonths and EveryNDays, anchored on the start of each contiguous run of terms so there is no month-end drift, and with no cycles in the gaps between terms. Each due date is then matched against the user's real activity (expenses plus unlinked debit bank-statement rows) using a date tolerance window and the amount range of the term covering that date. The match prefers a candidate with the same merchant, then the closest date, and a charge can satisfy only one cycle. Every cycle gets one status: Matched (with the source, id and actual date, flagged late when charged after the due date but inside the window), Retried (more than one charge attempt in the window), Missing (the window has closed with no match) or Upcoming. The result is computed on every read and never stored. The tolerance is one server config value (default 5 days on either side of the due date).

The only new persisted state is a manual payment log for cash, portal or manual-transfer subscriptions that never produce a bank row. It is a new user-scoped table with a cascade FK to the subscription. A manual payment satisfies the cycle it falls in and counts as Matched. The date+amount matcher is a single generic, pure component (slot = target date + optional amount range + optional merchant hint; candidate = id + date + amount + optional merchant). Row-to-receipt matching can reuse it later, but it is wired only to subscriptions now.

The feature is exposed in four places: Tapir endpoints (read the reconciliation for all subscriptions or one; add and delete a manual payment), a read-only `subscription_reconciliation` MCP tool, and the existing SubscriptionsPage. On that page, missing, late and retried cycles are clearly visible, matched cycles are collapsed, and a validated inline form logs or removes a manual payment. Out of scope: term suggestions, receipt matching, and any change to how subscriptions are created or updated. The repo is public, so no PII may appear in code, tests, commits or PR text: no real names, real amounts or account digits.

tasks.title: Shared due-date schedule in lib/api/shared
tasks.description: Create `lib/api/shared/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/api/utils/SubscriptionSchedule.scala`, a pure object built from the cadence math that today lives only in the web file `SubscriptionStatusLogic` (`web/.../pages/subscriptions/SubscriptionStatus.scala`): coveringTerm, nextTerm, cadenceAnchor (start of the contiguous run of terms), and the k-th occurrence from an anchor for each cadence. Every occurrence is computed from the anchor, never from the previous occurrence, so month-end clamping does not drift (31 Jan -> 28 Feb -> 31 Mar). Add `dueDates(terms, cadence, intervalDays, intervalMonths, today): Either[String, List[DueDate]]`, where `DueDate(date, term)`. It returns every occurrence d with a covering term (half-open [effectiveFrom, effectiveTo)) and d <= today, plus the first covered occurrence after today if there is one. Each run of adjacent terms keeps one anchor, and a gap (cancel then resume) starts a new anchor at the resumed term. No dates fall inside gaps. A missing or non-positive interval returns Left; never default it. Make the web `SubscriptionStatusLogic` delegate its coveringTerm/nextTerm/cadenceAnchor/latestOccurrence math to the shared object while keeping its public signatures and `SubscriptionStatusError`, so the existing `SubscriptionStatusLogicSpec` passes unchanged. Add `lib/api/shared/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/api/utils/SubscriptionScheduleSpec.scala` covering: Monthly 31st clamping without drift, Yearly from 29 Feb, EveryNMonths (2 and 3), EveryNDays, a price change keeping the anchor, a cancel/resume gap producing no dates and re-anchoring, a future-only term (only the upcoming date), and a missing interval -> Left. Verify with `sbt "apiJVM/testOnly *SubscriptionScheduleSpec"` (check build.sbt for the exact project id) and `sbt "web/testOnly *SubscriptionStatusLogicSpec"`.

tasks.title: Generic pure date+amount matcher
tasks.description: Add `lib/api/shared/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/api/utils/DateAmountMatcher.scala`, a pure object with no DB or HTTP. Generic inputs: `Slot[S](id: S, targetDate: LocalDate, amountRange: Option[(BigDecimal, BigDecimal)], merchantHint: Option[UUID])` and `Candidate[C](id: C, date: LocalDate, amount: BigDecimal, merchantId: Option[UUID])`, plus `toleranceDays: Int`. A pair is eligible when |date - targetDate| <= tolerance, the amount is inside the inclusive range when there is one, and the merchants are compatible: if both are set they must be equal. A slot with neither a range nor a hint only accepts candidates whose merchant equals... none, so it accepts nothing; this is deliberate, with no silent wildcard. Assignment: (1) greedy one-to-one primary matching over all eligible pairs, ordered by merchant equal to the hint first, then smaller |day difference|, then earlier slot date, then the ids for determinism; each slot gets at most one primary and each candidate is used at most once. (2) Every still-unused eligible candidate becomes an extra attempt of the matched slot it is eligible for with the nearest target date, but only when that slot belongs to the same group (take a `group: Slot => G` key; subscriptions pass the subscription id), so a retry is never credited across subscriptions. Return a result per slot (`primary: Option[Candidate]`, `extraAttempts: List[Candidate]`, ordered by date then id), so the caller can tell Matched, Retried and unmatched apart. Add `DateAmountMatcherSpec` in lib/api/shared tests covering: the exact window edges (tolerance in, tolerance+1 out, both sides), amount range edges, a merchant mismatch rejected, a missing candidate merchant accepted, the merchant preference beating a closer date on a same-amount collision, the closest date winning with no merchant, no double use across two slots, retries grouped within a group only, deterministic tie-breaks, and empty inputs. Use made-up generic data only.

tasks.title: Reconciliation API models and pure SubscriptionReconciler
tasks.description: Add the API models in `lib/api/shared/.../api/models/subscriptions/`: `SubscriptionChargeSource` enum (Expense, BankStatementRow, ManualPayment), following the SubscriptionCadence entryName/Format/Schema pattern; `SubscriptionCharge(source, id: UUID, date: LocalDate, amount: BigDecimal)`; `SubscriptionCycleStatus` enum whose variants carry their own data: `Matched(charge: SubscriptionCharge, late: Boolean)`, `Retried(attempts: List[SubscriptionCharge])`, `Missing`, `Upcoming`. Encode it as a tagged JSON object with a `kind` field like `ImportRuleAction`, using `Schema.derived`. Also add `SubscriptionCycle(dueDate, termId, amountMin, amountMax, status)`, `SubscriptionManualPayment(id, paidDate, amount, note: Option[SubscriptionManualPaymentNote])` (create the `lib/common` primitive here if the persistence task has not added it yet: trimmed, max 255, blank -> None via `parseOptional`, with a spec) and `GetSubscriptionReconciliation.Response(data: List[GetSubscriptionReconciliation.Response.Subscription(subscriptionId, cycles, manualPayments)])`. Declare implicit Formats and Schemas on the outer object as GetSubscriptions does, to avoid the static-init cycle. Use no default params. Then add `api/utils/SubscriptionReconciler.scala`, a pure function `reconcile(subscriptions: List[ReconcilerInput.Subscription(id, cadence, intervalDays, intervalMonths, merchantId, terms)], manualPayments, candidates: List[ReconcilerInput.Charge(source, id, date, amount, merchantId)], today, toleranceDays): Either[String, List[...Response.Subscription]]`. It expands due dates with SubscriptionSchedule and works in three steps. (a) Manual payments: each is assigned to a cycle of its own subscription whose bucket [due_i - tol, due_{i+1} - tol) contains the paid date, one payment per cycle, earliest first. Those cycles become Matched(ManualPayment, late = paidDate after dueDate) and are removed from bank matching. (b) Every other cycle becomes a DateAmountMatcher slot with the covering term's amount range and the subscription's merchant, grouped by subscription; all subscriptions are matched together so same-amount collisions resolve globally. (c) Status: a primary with extras -> Retried(primary plus the extras, by date); a primary alone -> Matched(late = actual date after due date); none and dueDate + tol < today -> Missing; otherwise Upcoming. Cycles are ordered by dueDate. Manual payments are always listed, ordered by paidDate then id. Add `SubscriptionReconcilerSpec` covering: on time, late inside the window, just outside the window -> Missing, a window still open -> Upcoming, retried, a same-amount collision resolved by merchant then by date, no double use across cycles and subscriptions, a cancel/resume gap with a charge inside the gap not flagged and not consumed, EveryNMonths, Yearly, a manual payment satisfying a cycle (and only one), and an unknown amount with no merchant matched only by a manual payment. Also add a JSON round-trip test for SubscriptionCycleStatus.

tasks.title: Manual payment persistence, validation and add/delete actions
tasks.description: Add evolution `server/src/main/resources/evolutions/default/20.sql`, in the 19.sql style (`-- !Ups` only, intent comments, NO semicolons inside `--` comments, no CHECK constraints). It creates `subscription_manual_payment` (id UUID PK, user_id UUID NOT NULL FK users(user_id), subscription_id UUID NOT NULL FK subscription(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, paid_date DATE NOT NULL, amount NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL, note TEXT NULL, created_at/updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL) with BTREE indexes on user_id and subscription_id. Add the `lib/common/shared/.../common/models/SubscriptionManualPaymentNote.scala` primitive (WrappedString, trimmed, MaxLength 255, `parseOptional`, with a spec) unless it already exists. In `SubscriptionValidator`, add `MaxManualPaymentsPerSubscription = 500` and `validateManualPaymentAmount` (same rules as validateExtraChargeAmount). Add the server model `repositories/models/SubscriptionManualPayment.scala` and `daos/SubscriptionManualPaymentDAO.scala`: create, countForSubscription, allForUser (ORDER BY subscription_id, paid_date, id), delete (`WHERE id AND subscription_id AND user_id`, 0 rows -> "Manual payment not found"); parse the note with `.trusted` only in the row parser. In `SubscriptionsRepository`, add `addManualPayment(payment, maxPerSubscription)` (one transaction: `SubscriptionDAO.lockForUpdate` -> "Subscription not found", count cap -> "Maximum number of manual payments (500) reached", create), `deleteManualPayment(id, subscriptionId, userId)`, and `manualPayments(userId)`. Add the request models `AddSubscriptionManualPayment.Request(paidDate: LocalDate, amount: BigDecimal, note: Option[SubscriptionManualPaymentNote])` / `Response(id)` and `DeleteSubscriptionManualPayment.Response()` in lib/api/shared. Add the actions `AddSubscriptionManualPaymentAction` (validate the amount -> fail, time-ordered UUID, Chimney into the model) and `DeleteSubscriptionManualPaymentAction`, mirroring the extra-charge actions. Add integration specs `AddSubscriptionManualPaymentActionSpec` / `DeleteSubscriptionManualPaymentActionSpec` (RepositorySpec + withRepositories, random unique names): stores the payment, rejects an invalid amount, rejects another user's subscription, enforces the 500 cap, cascades on subscription delete, a delete by another user fails and leaves the row, deleting an unknown id fails.

tasks.title: Reconciliation config, data read and GetSubscriptionReconciliationAction
tasks.description: Extend `server/.../config/SubscriptionsConfig.scala` to `SubscriptionsConfig(maxPerUser: Int, reconciliationToleranceDays: Int)` and add `reconciliationToleranceDays = 5` with `${?SUBSCRIPTIONS_RECONCILIATION_TOLERANCE_DAYS}` under `subscriptions {}` in application.conf. Fix the existing constructor calls (CreateSubscriptionActionSpec and anything else Test/compile flags). Add a read in `SubscriptionsRepository`, `reconciliationData(userId, from: LocalDate, to: LocalDate)`, done in one `withTransaction`. It returns the subscriptions with their terms (reuse SubscriptionDAO.all, SubscriptionTermDAO.allForUser), the manual payments, and the candidates: user expenses with date in [from, to] (new `ExpenseDAO` query, `WHERE user_id = ?`, ORDER BY date, id, positive amount plus merchant_id) and bank statement rows in [from, to] that are debits (`amount < 0`, reported as `-amount`) with `expense_id IS NULL AND refund_id IS NULL AND ignored_at IS NULL`. Rows are scoped via `JOIN bank_statement bs ... WHERE bs.user_id = ?` because bank_statement_row has no user_id column, ORDER BY date, id, and have no merchant. Linked rows are excluded because their expense already represents the charge. Add `actions/subscriptions/GetSubscriptionReconciliationAction(subscriptionsRepository, subscriptionsConfig)(implicit ec, clock)`, `apply(userId, subscriptionId: Option[UUID])`. today = LocalDate.now(clock); from = earliest term start - tol, to = today + tol. It always reconciles ALL of the user's subscriptions, so collisions resolve consistently, then filters to the requested one; an unknown or foreign id fails with "Subscription not found", and a Left from the reconciler fails the Future. Map rows to ReconcilerInput with Chimney where fields line up. Add `GetSubscriptionReconciliationActionSpec` (PostgresSpec/RepositorySpec, real DB, fixed Clock, random data, any needed RepositoryUtils helper for a bank statement row through `createStatement`). Cover: an expense matched, an unlinked debit row matched, a linked row not double-counted, a credit/ignored row ignored, missing, late, retried, a manual payment matched, a single-subscription filter, another user's expenses/rows/subscriptions never visible, and a foreign subscription id -> error.

tasks.title: Tapir endpoints, controller wiring and ApiClient
tasks.description: In `lib/api/shared/.../endpoints/SubscriptionsEndpoints.scala`, add: `getReconciliation` = GET /subscriptions/reconciliation with optional query `subscriptionId: Option[UUID]` -> GetSubscriptionReconciliation.Response (declare it before any `/subscriptions/{id}` GET so the paths cannot clash); `addManualPayment` = POST /subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/manual-payments with jsonBody AddSubscriptionManualPayment.Request; `deleteManualPayment` = DELETE /subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/manual-payments/{manualPaymentId}. Add the matching `ApiClient` methods (`getSubscriptionReconciliation(subscriptionId: Option[UUID])`, `addSubscriptionManualPayment`, `deleteSubscriptionManualPayment`). Wire them in `server/src/main/scala/controllers/SubscriptionsController.scala`: inject the 3 actions, add handlers that log `userId` and `subscriptionId` (never the note or amount), and add serverLogic entries. ApiRouter picks them up via `SubscriptionsEndpoints.routes` and `subscriptionsController.routes`, so confirm no further change is needed. Extend `server/src/test/scala/controllers/SubscriptionsControllerSpec.scala` with Mockito mocks bound via Guice overrides, covering auth and encoding only: unauthenticated -> error with verifyNoInteractions; authenticated -> the decoded request and ids reach the action and the result is encoded back (including a non-trivial SubscriptionCycleStatus payload with each variant, so the JSON round-trips); an action failure -> error message.

tasks.title: MCP subscription_reconciliation tool
tasks.description: In `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/mcp/McpTools.scala`, add `SubscriptionReconciliation = "subscription_reconciliation"` with a title, a noArgsSchema and a precise description. It should say that it returns, for every subscription, the per-cycle statuses (dueDate, termId, the amount range, and status kind Matched with source/id/date/amount/late, Retried with attempts, Missing, Upcoming) plus the logged manual payments. resultJson.brief:
REPO / PROJECT: Scala 3, sbt multi-project. Public repo, so no PII anywhere: use generic names ("Gym", "Streaming"), made-up amounts, no account digits. Issue owner/repo: AlexITC/expense-tracker (#130 open epic, #166 phase 2 closed). Verify only with targeted `sbt "testOnly *XSpec"` or `CI=true sbt Test/compile` (-Werror; unused imports fail). Run `sbt scalafmtAll scalafmtSbt` before committing. Web tests need Node 24 on PATH (the default node is v16). Never run the full `sbt test` inside a task.

LAYERS
- lib/common/shared/.../common/models/: validated WrappedString primitives (pattern: SubscriptionExtraChargeLabel.scala, SubscriptionDescription.scala with `parseOptional(raw: Option[String]): Either[String, Option[T]]` via `ValidationResults.toEither`). `.trusted` only in tests and DAO row parsing. Specs in lib/common/shared/src/test (e.g. SubscriptionExtraChargeLabelSpec).
- lib/api/shared/.../api/models/subscriptions/: request/response models. Pattern: case classes + `implicit Format` (Json.format) + `Schema.derived[...].name(Schema.SName("UniqueName"))`. Import `net.wiringbits.api.models.*` and `wrappedStringSchema` when a WrappedString field is used. Nested response types: declare their Format/Schema on the OUTER object (see GetSubscriptions.scala comment about the static-init cycle). Enums: `enum X(val entryName: String)` + `fromEntryName` + a Format that Reads the string + `Schema.string` (SubscriptionCadence.scala). An enum with data: tagged `kind` JSON Format like api/models/merchants/ImportRuleAction.scala. NO default parameter values in models (reviewer rule).
- lib/api/shared/.../api/utils/: pure shared logic, cross-compiled for JVM and JS, tested in lib/api/shared/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/api/utils/ (SubscriptionTermsSpec, ImportRuleMatcherSpec). SubscriptionTerms.scala: term-history rules, terms are half-open [effectiveFrom, effectiveTo), only the last may be open. SubscriptionValidator.scala: MaxAmountScale=2, MaxAmountIntegerDigits=10, MaxExtraChargesPerSubscription=50, `validateExtraChargeAmount(amount): Either[String, Unit]` (messages like "Amount must be greater than zero"), private validateAmount(label, amount).
- lib/api/shared/.../api/endpoints/SubscriptionsEndpoints.scala: `baseEndpoint = endpoint.in("subscriptions").tag("Subscriptions").errorOut(errorResponseErrorOut)`; each endpoint is `def x(implicit authHandler: ServerRequest => Future[UUID])` with `.in(path[UUID]("subscriptionId"))`, `.in(jsonBody[...])`, `.in(userAuth)`, `.out(jsonBody[...])`, `.errorOut(oneOf(HttpErrors.badRequest))`, `.summary(...)`, and is listed in `routes`. Existing GET paths: /subscriptions and /subscriptions/start-date-suggestion/{merchantId}. lib/api/shared/.../api/ApiClient.scala (~line 430) has `handleRequest(SubscriptionsEndpoints.x, (args..., dummyUserId))`.
- server/: controllers/SubscriptionsController.scala (injects actions; private handlers wrapped in `handleRequest { for { userId <- userIdF; _ = logger.info(s"... userId=$userId, subscriptionId=$id"); r <- action(...) } yield Right(r) }`; `routes` lists `Endpoint.serverLogic(handler)`). net/wiringbits/routing/ApiRouter.scala already includes SubscriptionsEndpoints.routes and subscriptionsController.routes, so new endpoints need no router edit.
- Actions: server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/actions/subscriptions/. Pattern: AddSubscriptionExtraChargeAction (`@Inject()(repo)(implicit ec: ExecutionContext, clock: Clock)`, validate via SubscriptionValidator -> `Future.failed(new RuntimeException(msg))`, `UuidCreator.getTimeOrderedEpoch()`, Chimney `.into[Model].withFieldConst(...).transform`). GetSubscriptionsAction maps repository rows with Chimney.
- Repository: server/.../repositories/SubscriptionsRepository.scala (`@Inject()(database: Database)(implicit ec: DatabaseExecutionContext, clock: Clock)`). Writes use `database.withTransaction`. The cap pattern is `addExtraCharge(charge, maxPerSubscription)`: `SubscriptionDAO.lockForUpdate(id, userId).isEmpty -> throw "Subscription not found"`, count, `throw "Maximum number of extra charges ($max) reached"`, create. `all(userId)` returns `Subscription.WithDetails(subscription, terms, extraCharges)` via SubscriptionDAO.all, SubscriptionTermDAO.allForUser and SubscriptionExtraChargeDAO.allForUser grouped by subscriptionId. Ownership is enforced inside the repository/DAO WHERE clause, not by an action pre-find (reviewer rule).
- DAOs: server/.../repositories/daos/. SubscriptionExtraChargeDAO.scala is the template (Anorm `SQL"""..."""`, `${id.toString}::UUID`, delete with `executeUpdate() == 0 -> throw "... not found"`, list `ORDER BY subscription_id, due_date, id`). Parsers live in daos/package.scala (`Macro.parser`, enum Columns via `Column.columnToString.map(X.fromEntryName)`). ExpenseDAO: table `expense(id, user_id, amount NUMERIC(12,2) positive, date, time, merchant_id NULL, notes, ...)`. BankStatementRowDAO: `bank_statement_row` has NO user_id; scope via `JOIN bank_statement bs ON bsr.bank_statement_id = bs.id WHERE bs.user_id = ?`. Row amount is signed (NEGATIVE = debit/money out, positive = credit); `expense_id`/`refund_id`/`ignored_at` are nullable. A row with expense_id set duplicates that expense, so exclude it from candidates.
- Evolutions: server/src/main/resources/evolutions/default/, latest is 19.sql, so the next is 20.sql. Style: `-- !Ups` only, explanatory comments, `CONSTRAINT <table>_id_pk PRIMARY KEY`, `<table>_user_id_fk FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES users(user_id)`, `<table>_subscription_id_fk ... resultJson.title: Reconcile subscription charges against expenses, bank rows and manual payments
resultJson.body:
Phase 3 of #130, following phase 2 (#166, PR #169). For each subscription, the app now shows whether every expected charge actually happened.

- **Derived on read, not stored.** Due dates come from the subscription's terms and cadence. They are matched against the user's expenses and unlinked debit bank statement rows. Each cycle is Matched (flagged late when charged after the due date), Retried, Missing or Upcoming. Gaps between terms (cancel then resume) produce no cycles, so cancelled periods are never flagged. One charge can satisfy only one cycle. When two subscriptions have the same amount, the merchant match wins first, then the closest date.
- **Shared pure logic in `lib/api/shared`.** `DateAmountMatcher` is generic (slots and candidates), so row-to-receipt matching can reuse it later. `SubscriptionSchedule` holds the cadence math that used to live only in the web `SubscriptionStatusLogic`, which now delegates to it. `SubscriptionReconciler` combines the two.
- **Manual payment log.** This is the only new persisted state, for cash, portal or manual-transfer subscriptions that never produce a bank row. Evolution `20.sql` adds a user-scoped table with a cascading FK to the subscription. Limits: max 500 payments per subscription, note max 255 chars, amount validated like other subscription amounts. A manual payment counts as Matched for the cycle it falls in.
- **Config.** The tolerance window is one server setting: `subscriptions.reconciliationToleranceDays`, default 5 days on either side of the due date.
- **API, MCP and web.** New endpoints: `GET /subscriptions/reconciliation` (optional `subscriptionId`), and POST/DELETE `/subscriptions/{id}/manual-payments`. There is a new read-only `subscription_reconciliation` MCP tool. `SubscriptionsPage` shows missing, late and retried cycles, collapses on-time ones, and has a validated form to log or remove a manual payment.

Notes for reviewers:
- Reconciliation always runs over all of the user's subscriptions, then filters when one is requested, so same-amount collisions resolve the same way in both cases.
- Bank rows already linked to an expense are excluded, so the charge isn't counted twice.
- A cycle whose term has no amount range and whose subscription has no merchant can only be satisfied by a manual payment.
- Past due dates are capped at 366 per run of terms, so a very old start date can't generate an unbounded list.

Out of scope: term suggestions, receipt matching, and any change to how subscriptions are created or updated.
